translations.text: Love righteousness, you who judge the earth. Think of the Lord with goodness, and seek him with a sincere heart.
For he is found by those who do not put him to the test, and he reveals himself to those who do not doubt him.
For crooked thoughts separate people from God, and his power, when put to the test, exposes the foolish.
For wisdom will not enter a soul that devises evil, nor dwell in a body ruled by sin.
For the Holy Spirit of wisdom will flee from deceit, withdraw from foolish thoughts, and rebuke injustice when it arises.

For the Spirit of wisdom loves humanity, but will not acquit a blasphemer for what his lips say, because God is a witness to his innermost feelings, a true observer of his heart, and a listener to his tongue.
For the Spirit of the Lord fills the world, and the one who holds all things together knows every utterance.
Therefore those who whisper unjust things will not remain hidden, nor will justice pass them by without rebuke.
For the thoughts of the ungodly will be questioned and examined, and a report of their words will reach the Lord, to rebuke their lawless deeds.
For the ear of jealousy hears everything, and whispered grumbling will not remain hidden.
From now on, beware of useless grumbling, and keep your tongue from slander, for a secret whisper will not pass without consequence, and a lying mouth kills the soul.
Do not desire death through the waywardness of your lives, and do not draw destruction upon yourselves through the works of your hands.
For God did not make death, and he does not rejoice in the destruction of living things.
For he established all things so that they might exist, and the things made in the world serve preservation. There is no deadly poison in them, nor does Hades reign upon the earth.
For righteousness is immortal.
But the ungodly summoned death to themselves by their deeds and words. They regarded it as a friend and wasted away, and they made a covenant with it, for they are indeed worthy to share in it.
They thought crooked thoughts to themselves and said, “Our lives are short and painful, and there is no remedy at a person's end, nor has anyone been seen returning from Hades.
For we came into being by chance, and afterward we will be as though we had never existed. For the breath in our nostrils is like smoke, and speech is like a spark in the beating of our heart.
When it is extinguished, the body becomes ashes, and the spirit disperses like thin air.

Our name will be forgotten in time, and no one will remember our deeds. Our lives will pass like the traces of a cloud and disperse like mist, driven away by the rays of the sun and weighed down by its heat.
For our lives are the passing of a shadow, and there is no stopping the end of humanity, because it has been sealed, and no one can reverse it.
Come, then, let us enjoy the good things that are here, and eagerly make use of created things as in our youth.
Let us fill ourselves with various wines and fragrant oils; let no spring blossom pass us by.
Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.
Let no one be left out of our lavish revelry. Everywhere let us leave signs of our joy, for this is our portion and this is our lot.
Let us unjustly oppress the poor man; let us not spare the widow or show reverence for the gray hair of the aged.”
Let our strength be the law of righteousness, for weakness proves to be useless.
Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he has become troublesome to us and opposes our deeds. He reproaches us for transgressions of the law and accuses us of the sins of our youth.
He claims to have knowledge of God and calls himself a son of the Lord.
And he has become a rebuke to our thoughts.
Even seeing him is burdensome to us, because his life is unlike that of others, and his paths are different.
He considers us an abomination and avoids our ways as though they were impurities. He calls the end of the righteous blessed and proudly calls God his Father.
Let us see whether his words are true, and let us put his end to the test.
If he truly is a son of God, God will defend him and rescue him from the hands of his adversaries.
Let us torment him with insults and beatings, to see whether he will receive help, so that we may measure his gentleness and understand his freedom from resentment.
Let us condemn him to a shameful death, to see whether he will receive help, as his own words claim.
They reasoned this way and were deceived, because their own wickedness blinded them.
They did not know God's purposes, did not expect a reward for holiness, and did not recognize the honor of blameless souls.
For God established humanity for incorruptibility and made humanity in the image of his own goodness.
Through the devil's envy, death entered the world.
And those who belong to his portion experience it.
But the souls of the righteous are in God's hand, and death will not approach them.
In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died, and their departure was considered suffering.
And their leaving us was considered destruction, but they are at peace.
For although they suffered torment in human eyes, their hope is full of immortality.
After a little discipline and sorrow, they will find great goodness, because God tested them and found them worthy of himself.
He tested them like gold in a furnace and accepted them like a sacrificial burnt offering. At the time of their visitation,
They will shine and run like sparks through reeds.
They will judge nations and take possession of peoples, and the Lord will reign over them forever.
Those who trust in him will understand the truth, and the faithful will look to him in love, because grace and mercy are upon his holy ones, and his care is upon his chosen ones.
But the ungodly will receive punishment according to their own designs, because they neglected justice and rebelled against the Lord.
For whoever despises wisdom and instruction is miserable. Their hope is empty, their labors are fruitless, and their deeds are useless.
Their wives are foolish, and their children are wicked.
And their offspring are cursed. For blessed is the blameless barren woman who has not known a sinful bed; she will receive fruit at the visitation of souls.

And the eunuch who has committed no lawlessness with his hands and has thought no evil against the Lord will be given a choice gift according to his faith and a desirable portion in the Lord's temple.
For the fruit of good labors is glorious, and the root that springs from wisdom never fails.
The children of adulterers will remain incomplete, and the offspring of unlawful beds will perish.
Even if they live long, they will be considered worthless, and their old age will be dishonored at its end.
And if they perish quickly, they will have no hope and no comfort on the day of judgment.
For the end of an unrighteous family is grievous.
Childlessness with virtue is better, because its memory is immortal, for it is recognized both by God and by people.
When it is present, people imitate it, and when it departs, they long for it. Forever it parades crowned, having triumphed in the battle of unfading contests.
The numerous offspring of the ungodly will be useless. From their rotten shoots they will not put down deep roots, nor will an unstable root and foundation become established.
For even if it buds with branches for a time, its frail [?] will be shaken by the wind and uprooted by the force of the wind.
The immature shoots around it will be broken off, and their fruit will be useless, too unripe for food and fit for nothing.
For children born of unlawful beds are witnesses to their parents’ wickedness when they are examined.
But the righteous person, if he comes to die, will be at rest.
For honorable old age does not consist in a long span of time, nor is it measured by the number of years; rather, a person’s wisdom is his gray hair,
and a blameless life is the stature of old age.
For he pleased God and was loved, and while still living he was taken away from among sinners.
He was snatched away so that no wickedness would overturn his wisdom or deceit beguile his soul.
For the malice of foolishness obscures what is good, and the wandering of desire throws innocent minds into confusion.
Made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled many years,
because his soul was pleasing to the Lord. Therefore he was hurried away from among the wicked. But the peoples saw and did not understand, nor did they take such a thing to heart.
For God's judgment is upon his holy ones, and his visitation is upon his chosen ones.
The righteous person who has died condemns the ungodly who are living, and youth that has quickly reached its end condemns the many years of an unrighteous person’s old age.
For they will see the wise person’s end and will not understand what the Lord planned for him or what he protected him from.
They will see him and despise him, but the Lord will laugh at them.

After this they will fall into dishonor and become an object of contempt among the dead forever. For he will burst them, puffed up and speechless, and shake them from their foundations. They will be utterly laid waste and will suffer pain, and their memory will perish.
They will come in anguish to face their accumulated sins, and their lawless deeds will openly rebuke them.
Then the righteous person will stand with great confidence before those who oppressed him and those who despised his labors.
When they see him, they will be shaken with overwhelming fear and astonished at his wonderful deliverance.
They will feel remorse in their minds and groan in the anguish of their souls, and say, “This is the man whom we once mocked and made a byword of reproach.
We fools considered his way of life madness and his end dishonorable.
How was he counted among the children of God, and how is his lot among the saints?
So we strayed from the path of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine on us, and the sun of righteousness did not rise in our hearts.
We had our fill of the paths of lawlessness and destruction, and traveled through an untrodden wilderness, but we did not know the ways of the Lord.
What profit did our pride bring us, and what benefit could the grandeur of our arrogance give us?
All that passed like a shadow and like the report of a man running past.
And like a ship gliding through swelling waters, once it has passed, no trace can be found, nor any track of its passage among the waves;

or like a bird flying through the air, whose passage leaves no visible traces: beating its claws, it tears the light wind and, cleaving it with force, passes through its expanses; with the movement of its wings it darts forward, and afterward no sign of its flight can be found there;
or like an arrow shot at a target: the air it cuts through immediately closes together again, so that its passage cannot be known.
So we too came into being and passed away, and could show no sign of virtue, but wasted away in our wickedness.”

For the hope of the ungodly is like dust stirred up by the wind, like a spider’s web and frost that melts and crumbles in a storm, like smoke dispersed by the wind, or like the memory of a guest who stayed for one day and departed.
But the righteous will live forever, and their reward is from the Lord, and their care is from the Most High.
Therefore they will receive a glorious kingdom and a beautiful crown from the hand of the Lord, for he will shelter them with his right hand and watch over them with his arm.
He will take his zeal as his full armor and arm creation to exact vengeance on his enemies.
He will put on righteousness as a breastplate and place impartial judgment on his head as a helmet.
He will take holiness as an unyielding shield.
He will sharpen his fierce anger into a sword, and the world will join him in battle against the foolish.
Mighty arrows of lightning will fly, and leap from the clouds toward their targets as from a fully drawn bow.
Hail will pour down abundantly from the sling of his wrath. The water of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will overwhelm them without mercy.
A mighty wind will strike them head-on and sweep them away like a whirlwind. Lawlessness will devastate the whole earth, and deceit will overthrow the thrones of rulers.
Listen, kings, and understand; learn, judges of the ends of the earth.
Give ear, you who rule over multitudes and boast over crowds of nations.
For your dominion was given to you by the Lord, and your authority by the Most High, who will call your deeds to account and examine your plans.
For you are servants of his kingdom, but you do not judge uprightly, have not kept his laws, and have not walked according to the will of God.
He will come upon you with terror and anguish, for rulers face impartial judgment.
But the ordinary person can be pardoned through mercy; the powerful will be called to account more severely.
For the Lord of all shows no partiality and does not shrink before greatness, because he himself made both the small and the great, and he cares for everyone alike.
But a severe examination will come upon the powerful.
So my words are addressed to you, rulers, so that you may learn wisdom and not go astray.
For those who have kept holy things in holiness will be made holy, and those who have learned them will find a defense.
Therefore desire my words, long for them, and receive instruction.
Wisdom is radiant and unfading. She is easily seen by those who love her and found by those who seek her.
She comes to those who desire her, making herself known beforehand.
Whoever rises early to seek her will not grow weary, for he will find her waiting at his doors.
For even to think about her is perfect wisdom, and whoever keeps watch for her will soon be free from care.
For she herself goes about seeking those worthy of her. She appears to them graciously on their paths and meets them in all their endeavors.
For her beginning is a true desire for instruction.
And care for instruction is love, and love is the keeping of her laws; confidence in the laws is an assurance of incorruptibility.
And incorruptibility brings one near to God.
And the desire for wisdom leads to a kingdom.
Therefore, if you desire thrones and scepters of authority, rulers of peoples, honor wisdom so that you may reign forever.

But I will explain what wisdom is and how she came to be, and I will not hide her mysteries from you. Rather, I will investigate from the beginning of creation and bring knowledge of her to light. I will not turn aside from the truth.
Nor will I make consuming envy my companion, for it has no fellowship with wisdom.
A multitude of wise people is the salvation of the world, and an intelligent king is the stability of his people.
Therefore, be instructed by my words and benefit from them.
I too am indeed a mortal human being, like everyone else, and a descendant of the first-created man, born from the earth. In my mother's womb I was formed into flesh.
And over ten months I took shape in blood, from a man's seed and from the pleasure that accompanied sleep.
When I was born, I too drew in the air common to all and fell upon the same earth, sharing the same suffering. My first sound, like everyone else's, was likewise a cry.
I was raised in swaddling clothes and with care.
No king had any different beginning to his existence.
There is one entrance into the world for everyone, and one departure common to all.
Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given to me; I called, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
I preferred her to powers and thrones, and considered wealth nothing in comparison with her.
I did not compare precious stones with her, for all gold beside her is like a little sand, and silver will be considered clay before her.
I loved her more than health and beauty, and chose to have her rather than light, for the light that comes from her never sleeps.
All good things came to me together with her, and countless riches were in her hands.
I rejoiced in all the things that wisdom led, but I did not know that she was their mother.
I learned without deceit, and I will share without envy; I will not hide her riches.
For she is an unfailing treasure for humanity. Those who made use of her offered friendship to God, being commended because of the gifts received through instruction.
But may God grant me to speak with understanding and to think in a manner worthy of the words spoken, for he himself is both the guide of wisdom and the one who directs the wise.
For in his hand are both we and our words, and all understanding and skill in work.
For he gave me unerring knowledge of things that exist, to know the structure of the world and the workings of the elements.
The beginning, the end, and the middle of times, the changes of cycles, and the turning of seasons;
The cycles of years and the positions of stars;
The habits of animals and the ferocity of wild beasts, the force of winds and human speech, the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.
I came to know whatever is hidden and whatever is visible, for wisdom, the architect of all things, taught me.
For in her there is a spirit that is intelligent, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, readily moving, clear, undefiled, manifest, unerring, loving what is good, swift, unhindered, and beneficent;
Loving humanity, steadfast, watchful, free from care, all-powerful, all-seeing, and capable of encompassing all things that are intelligent, holy, and subtle.
Wisdom moves more readily than anything that moves; she orders and penetrates everything because of her purity.
For she is a ray of God's power and a true emanation of the Almighty's glory; therefore nothing defiled mingles with her.
For she is the radiance of everlasting light, an unblemished mirror of God's activity, and an image of his abundance.
She is one and can do everything; remaining in herself, she renews everything, and passing into holy souls from generation to generation, she makes friends of God and prophets.
God loves no one except the one who lives with wisdom.
For she is more beautiful than the sun and than every arrangement of stars; compared with light, she is found superior.
For night takes the place of light, but evil does not overcome wisdom.
She stretches from end to end with beneficial strength and orders everything gently.
I loved her and sought her from my youth, and sought to take her as my bride, and became a lover of her beauty.
She glorifies her noble birth, for she shares life with God, and the Lord of all loved her.
For she is a confidante of God's wisdom and a lover of his beauty.
If wealth is a desirable possession in life, what could be greater than wisdom, which makes everything?
If understanding accomplishes anything, who among existing things is a more skillful craftsman than she?
If anyone loves righteousness, her labors are virtues, for she teaches knowledge and understanding, righteousness and courage, than which nothing is more useful in human life.

If anyone desires to be widely experienced, she knows the past and discerns what is to come. She understands turns of speech and interpretations of parables; she knows signs and arts beforehand, and the outcomes of times and seasons.
So I resolved to take her as my companion for life, knowing that she would counsel me in good things and comfort me in cares and sorrow.
Because of her I will have glory among the peoples and honor before the elders.
Though young, I will be found sharp in judgment, and I will be glorified in the eyes of the powerful.
When I am silent, they will wait for me; when I speak, they will look at me attentively; and when I speak at length, they will put their hands over their mouths.
Because of her I will have immortality and an everlasting remembrance among those whom I leave behind.
I will govern peoples, and nations will submit to me.
Fearsome tyrants will tremble at me when they hear of me. Among the multitude I will appear generous, and in war courageous.
When I enter my house, I will rest with her, for living with her brings no bitterness, and sharing her life brings no pain, but joy and gladness.
I considered these things within myself, reflecting in my heart that kinship with wisdom is immortality,

and that friendship with her brings enjoyment of good things, the labors of her hands bring inexhaustible wealth, training in her words brings understanding, and sharing in her discourse brings glory. And I went about seeking how I might take her to myself.
I was a youth with a well-trained mind, and I received a good spirit.
Rather, because I was nobler, I entered an undefiled body.

I knew that I could not otherwise be self-controlled unless God granted it. And this too is wisdom: to know from whom the gift comes. I fell down before the Lord and pleaded with him with all my heart.
God of the fathers and Lord of your mercy, you are the one who made everything by your word
and formed humanity by your wisdom, so that humanity might rule over the creatures made by you
and govern the world in holiness and righteousness, and render judgment with an upright spirit.
Give me the wisdom that sits beside your thrones, and do not reject me from among your servants.
For I am your servant and the son of your maidservant, a weak and short-lived man, deficient in understanding judgment and laws.
For even if someone is perfect among the children of men, if the wisdom that comes from you is far from him, he will be regarded as nothing.
You chose me as king of your people and judge of your sons and daughters.
You told me to build a temple on your holy mountain and an altar in the city where you dwell, in the likeness of the holy tabernacle that you prepared beforehand, from the beginning.
With you is wisdom, who knows your works and was present when you made the world. She knows what is pleasing in your eyes and what is right according to your commandments.
Send her from the holy heavens, and dispatch her from your glorious throne, so that she may come and dwell with me, and I may know what is pleasing before you.
For she knows and understands everything. She will guide me prudently in my deeds and guard me by her glory.
Then my deeds will be acceptable, and I will judge your people justly and be worthy of my father's throne.
For who is the person who can know God's counsel? Or who can conceive what the Lord desires?
For the thoughts of mortals are uncertain, and our plans are unstable.
For the perishable body weighs down the soul, and this earthly dwelling burdens the mind with its many cares.
We can barely discern earthly things, and we discover with difficulty what lies at our feet. But who can investigate what is in heaven?
And who has known your counsel unless you gave wisdom and sent your Holy Spirit from on high?
Then the paths of those on earth were made straight, people learned your ways, and they were saved by your wisdom.
She preserved the first-created father of the world, who had been created alone.
She rescued him from his transgressions and gave him strength to rule over everything.
But the unrighteous man turned away from her in his anger and perished in his murderous rage against his brother.
Because of him, wisdom again saved the flooded earth, steering the righteous man by means of a small piece of wood.
When the nations were thrown into confusion in their unity in evil, she recognized the righteous man and kept him blameless before God. She kept him strong in the face of compassion for his son.
She rescued the righteous man as he fled the destruction of the ungodly, when fire descended upon the five cities.
As a witness to their wickedness, the desolate land still lies smoking, with fruit-bearing plants whose fruit never ripens, and a pillar of salt stands as a memorial to an unbelieving soul.

For those who disregarded wisdom were not only harmed by failing to recognize what is good, but also left a memorial of their foolishness in the world, so that they could not conceal the things in which they sinned.
Wisdom rescued those who appealed to her from their sufferings.

She guided the righteous man along straight paths when he fled from his brother's anger. She showed him the kingdom of God and gave him knowledge of holy things. She prospered him with gains from his labors and multiplied the fruit of his work.
She defended him against the greed of his oppressors and made him great.

She protected him from enemies and guarded him against those who lay in ambush for him. In a fierce battle she made him victorious, so that he might know that devotion to God is stronger than anything else.
She did not abandon the righteous man who had been sold, but rescued him from sin. She went down with him into the pit.
Even in chains she did not abandon him, until she brought him a royal scepter and authority over his oppressors. She proved his accusers false and gave him everlasting glory.
She rescued a holy people and a blameless nation from a nation of oppressors.
She entered the soul of the Lord's servant and stood against fearsome kings through wonders and signs.
She paid the holy ones the reward for their labors and guided them along a marvelous path. She became a shelter for them by day and a flame of stars by night.
She led them through the Red Sea and brought them through mighty waters.
She drowned their enemies and brought them up from the depths of the abyss.
Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly and blessed your holy name, Lord, and together they praised your hand, which fought on their behalf.
For wisdom opened the mouths of the mute and made the tongues of children speak clearly.
She made their works prosper through the holy prophet.
They traveled through an uninhabited wilderness and pitched their tents in untrodden places.
They stood against those who fought them and drove away their enemies.
They thirsted and called upon you, and water was given to them from a rocky crag, and relief for their thirst from hard rock.
For the things by which their enemies were tormented
were the very things through which these people, in their need, received kindness.
For them, instead of the ever-flowing river, reddened with blood and disturbed,
as a rebuke for the command to slaughter children, you gave abundant water beyond all hope,
showing through their thirst at that time how you had tormented their adversaries.
When they received their measure of discipline, though they were corrected with mercy, they understood how the ungodly would be tormented when judged in anger.
You tested these people, correcting them like a father, but you rebuked the others, condemning them like a stern king.
Those far away and those nearby were in danger alike.
For a twofold sorrow seized them, and groaning over memories of the past.
For when they heard that others were benefiting through their own torments, they came to recognize your measure, Lord.

For the one whom they had cast out and rejected yesterday and long ago, and whom they mocked, they marveled at when those events reached their outcome, for their thirst was not like that of the righteous.

In return for their foolish schemes of wrongdoing, through which they went astray and worshiped speechless reptiles and vile insects, you sent a multitude of creatures without speech upon them as punishment.
So that they might know that the things through which someone sins are also the things through which that person is tormented.
For your almighty hand, which established the world from formless matter, did not lack the means to send upon them multitudes of bears or fierce lions,
or newly created, unknown beasts full of rage, or fire-breathing creatures [?] in their ferocity, or creatures pouring out putrid smoke, or creatures flashing fierce lightning from their eyes.
Not only could their harmful attacks have crushed them, but their very appearance could have killed them with terror.
Even without these, you could have destroyed them with a single gust, pursued by judgment and swept away by the breath of your power. But you arranged everything by measure, number, and weight.
For it is within your power to act with great might at any time, and who can resist the strength of your arm?
For the whole world before you is like a slight tipping of the scales, and like a drop of morning dew that falls to the earth.
But you have mercy on everyone, because you can do everything, and you overlook people's sins so that they may repent.
For you love everything that exists, and you do not despise anything you have made, for you did not establish anything out of hatred.
For how could anything exist if you did not will it? Or how could anything that had not been called by you be preserved?
Spare everyone, for they are yours, Lord, lover of souls.
For your incorruptible Spirit is in everyone.
Therefore you rebuke offenders little by little, and you admonish them by reminding them of the things in which they sin, so that, freed from evil, they may believe in you, Lord.
You also hated the ancient inhabitants of your holy land
because they practiced detestable deeds of sorcery and unholy sacrifices,
the merciless killers of children and the eaters of the entrails of human bodies, which they fed on, and of blood, from among your divine initiates.
And you wished to destroy the wealthy and the parents of helpless people by the hands of our fathers,
so that the land, which was more precious to you than any other, might be fittingly subjected to God's servants.
Yet you spared even them as human beings. You sent hornets as the advance guard of your army, so that they might destroy them little by little.
You were not powerless in battle to deliver the ungodly into the hands of the righteous, or to crush them with fearsome beasts, or all at once, in an instant, with a word.
But by judging them little by little, you gave them room for repentance, not being unaware that their conduct was evil, that their wickedness was inborn, and that their thoughts would never change.
For they were an accursed offspring from the beginning. It was not because you feared anyone that you granted forgiveness for the things in which they sinned.

For who will say to you, 'What have you done?' Or who will oppose your judgment? Who will reproach you for the destruction of nations that you created? Or who will come against you to avenge unrighteous people?
For there is no other God besides you who cares for everyone, to whom you should show that you have not judged unjustly.
Nor can any king or ruler lift his eyes against you on behalf of those whom you punished.
For you are righteous and govern everything with righteousness. You punished the one who deserved punishment, considering [?] foreign to your power.
For your power governs righteousness, and your dominion over everyone leads you to spare everyone.
You display strength against the doubter with perfect power, and you rebuke those who do not recognize your power.
You who rule with power judge with gentleness, and you care for us with great concern, for it is within your reach to exercise power whenever you wish.
Through such deeds you taught your people that the righteous must love humanity, and you gave your children good hope, because you grant repentance for sins.
For if you punished and saved the enemies of your servants, who deserved death, with such great forbearance, giving them times and opportunities through which they might escape evil,
you judged your children with complete truthfulness, those with whose fathers you made oaths and covenants promising good things.
Thus, while disciplining us, you punish our enemies ten thousandfold, so that we may consider the measure of your kindness and, when judged, expect mercy.
Therefore you also tormented those who lived unjustly in a life of folly through their own abominations.
For they wandered far along paths of error, regarding as gods creatures that were despised even among their animal enemies, deceived like foolish children.
For this reason, you passed judgment on them as on infants, making it a mockery.
And because they were not corrected by these mocking rebukes, they will undergo the judgment worthy of God.

For they will be tormented by the very things they regarded as gods, which made them angry when they suffered through them. Seeing the one whom they had previously denied, they recognized that he is the true God. For this reason, a sign of condemnation also came upon them.
For all people who were ignorant of God were vain by nature: from the good things they could see, they could not know the one who exists, nor did they recognize the craftsman by looking at his works.
Instead, they regarded as gods either fire, wind, swift air, the courses of the stars, the powerful waters, or the heavenly lights that govern the world.
If, delighted by their beauty, they consider them gods, let them know how much better their Lord is, for the creator of beauty himself established them.
But if they marvel at their power and activity, let them understand from these things how much more powerful the one who fashioned them is.
For from the greatness and beauty of created things, their maker can also be seen by comparison.
Yet there is still only a little blame for them, for perhaps they go astray while seeking God and wishing to find him.
Moving among his works, they examine them and are persuaded by their appearance that these visible things are beautiful.
Nevertheless, they too are not to be excused.
For if they were able to know enough to examine the world, how did they not quickly find the Lord of these things?

Wretched are those whose hope is in dead things, who regarded as gods the works of human hands: gold and silver, products of skilled craftsmanship, likenesses of animals, or a useless stone worked by ancient hands.
Suppose a carpenter sawed a fine piece of wood, skillfully scraped off all its bark, and cleverly fashioned a handsome vessel useful for the needs of life.
He used the shavings from his work to prepare food and ate his fill; and whatever among them was useless and discarded—
Taking the crooked wood, full of knots, he carved it with attention to his work and shaped it with thoughtful skill. He made it resemble a human figure.
Or he fashioned it in the likeness of a worthless animal. He coated it with [?], reddened its color with vermilion, and plastered all its [?] with clay.
He made a suitable house for it and placed it against a wall, securing it with iron.
He took care that it should not fall, knowing that it cannot even help itself, because it is an image and needs help.
Then he approaches it and whispers to the lifeless thing about his marriage, his children, and his possessions.
He begs it and feels no shame. For health he calls upon the powerless; for life he begs the dead; and for help he implores one who is itself at a loss.
For a journey he appeals to something that cannot even move one foot before the other; and for wealth, work, and strength of hand, he asks success from something whose hands can accomplish nothing.
Again, someone who boards a ship and wishes to travel through fearsome waves cries out to a piece of wood weaker than the wood of the ship.
For although the desire for profit devised the ship, and a craftsman skillfully constructed it,
nevertheless, Father, your providence steers it, for you have provided a path even in the sea and a safe passage through the waves,
showing that you can save from every danger, even if someone goes aboard without skill.
But you wish the work of wisdom not to be fruitless. Therefore people entrust their lives to a worthless piece of wood, and, crossing the waves on a small raft, they were saved.
For even in the beginning, when the arrogant giants were destroyed, the hope of the world took refuge on a wooden raft and left the world offspring for the future, steered by your hand.
For blessed is the wood through which righteousness comes about.
But the handmade object is cursed, both it and the one who made it: he because he made it, and it because, though perishable, it was called a god.
The ungodly person and his ungodliness are equally hateful to God.
For the work and its maker will be punished together.
Therefore punishment will also come upon the idols of the nations, because among God's creatures they became an abomination, stumbling blocks for human beings, and snares for the feet of the foolish.
For the devising of idols is the beginning of sexual immorality, and their invention is the corruption of life.
For they did not exist from the beginning, nor will they remain forever.
They entered the world through people's religious innovations, and therefore an end was devised for them that would come soon.

For a father, stricken with untimely grief, made an image of his son who had died prematurely. The man who was dead at that time he now honored as a god, and he handed down mysteries and offerings to those subject to him.
Then, as time passed, the ungodly custom was observed as a law, and carved images were appointed for worship by the commands of rulers.

Those whom people could not honor in person because they lived far away, they represented by carving and fashioning a likeness of their absent appearance. They made a visible image of the king they honored, so that they might eagerly flatter the distant ruler as though he were near.
Afterward, the craftsman's abundant skill encouraged the ignorant to increase their worship.
For he, perhaps wishing to please the ruler's mind, strained his skill to make the likeness beautiful.
But the multitude, deceived by the attractiveness of the work, now regarded as an object of worship the one whom, only a little earlier, they had honored as a man.
And this became a trap and a stumbling block in life. For people, enslaved at that time to the tyranny of grief, gave to stones and wood the name that cannot be shared.
And it was not enough for them to stray from the knowledge of God; while living in the great war of ignorance, they called such evils peace.
They performed either offerings in which children were killed, or secret mysteries, or frenzied debaucheries belonging to other religious rites.
They no longer keep either life or marriage pure. A man either kills his neighbor in confusion or secretly [?] him.
And everything is utterly confused: bloodshed and murder, theft and deceit, corruption, unfaithfulness, turmoil, perjury, uproar,
forgetfulness of benefits received, defilement of souls, confusion of parentage, disorder in marriages, adultery, lust.
For the naming and worship of idols is the beginning, cause, and culmination of every evil.
Either they rejoice and become frenzied, or they prophesy lies, or they live unjustly, or they rush into false oaths.
For, trusting in lifeless idols, they swear falsely and have no expectation of punishment.
So both punishments will rightly come upon them, because they thought wickedly about God, heeded idols, and swore falsely by idols, despising holiness.
For it is not the power of the things sworn by, but the judgment upon sinners, that brings the offenses of the unrighteous to their full consequence.
But you, our God, are kind and true, patient, and govern everything with mercy.
For even if we sin, we are yours, because we know your power. But we will not sin, because we know that we are under your command.
For knowing you is itself complete righteousness, and knowing your power is the root of immortality.
For neither the wicked ingenuity of human beings nor the fruitless labor of painters has led us astray—an artificially fashioned image in various colors.
The sight of these arouses desire in fools, who long for the image of something dead, a lifeless appearance.
Those who practice evil arts are worthy of such a hope, as are those who make these things, those who desire them, and those who worship them.

For a potter, kneading soft clay, places it on the wheel and fashions a vessel for each of our uses. From the same clay he fashions vessels for sacred service, or for ordinary work, or for purposes entirely opposite to these, all in the same manner. The potter is the judge of which of these meets each need, and [?].

For he vainly fashions a god from the same clay—he who was himself formed from the earth a little while ago, and after a short time returns to the place from which he was taken, when the debt of his soul is demanded.

But his concern is not that he will grow weary, nor that his life will soon end, but that he competes with goldsmiths and silversmiths, imitates bronzeworkers, and considers it glorious to fashion abominable things.
His heart is ashes, his hope is worthless earth, and his life is more dishonorable than clay.
For he did not recognize his Creator, nor the one who breathed into him the breath of activity and breathed into him a living spirit.
Instead, they considered our existence a game and our life a fair for making profits. For they say that one must gain something from whatever source, even from evil.
And he knows better than anyone that he is sinning when he makes fragile vessels and molded images from earthen material.
They are all utterly foolish and more helpless than the soul of a child. The enemies of your people oppressed them,

for they regarded all the idols of the nations as gods, though their eyes were of no use for seeing, nor their ears for hearing, nor their nostrils for drawing in air, nor the fingers of their hands for touching; and their feet were incapable of walking.
For a human being made them, and one with a borrowed spirit fashioned them. No human being can fashion a likeness of God,
for he is mortal and makes a dead work with lawless hands. He himself is better than the things he worships, since he is alive, while they never are.
They even worship the most repulsive animals, and this is incredible foolishness.

For if they are compared with other animals, they prove to be worse. Their forms do not possess the sort of beauty people desire in animals. But they have fallen away from the knowledge of God and from his blessing.
Therefore they were deservedly tormented by creatures like these and were scourged by a multitude of vermin.
In place of that torment, you brought relief to your people: to satisfy their longing, you prepared quail, a food of unfamiliar taste.
Thus, although the others desired food, the sights sent to them kept them from desiring even necessary food, while your people, after being in need for a little while, would enjoy a new taste.
For unavoidable deprivation had to come upon the others, because they acted as oppressors, while your people needed only to be shown how their enemies would be tormented.
For when the terrible fury of wild animals came upon these people, they were perishing from the bites of vicious snakes.
The anger did not last to the end, but they were troubled for a short time as a correction, so that they might have a sign of salvation to remind them of the commandments of your law.
For whoever turned toward it was saved not because of what he saw, but because of you, who are the Savior of all.
And by this you convinced our enemies that you are the one who saves from every evil.
For the attacks of locusts and mice killed some people, and no healing was found for them, because they deserved to be tormented by such creatures.
But not even the fangs of venomous serpents overcame your children, and your mercy stood between them and saved them.
For they were stung again to remind them of your words, and were quickly rescued, so that they would not fall into deep forgetfulness and be left without the protection of your kindness.
For neither medicines nor poultices healed them, but your word, Lord, which heals everything.
For you have authority over life and death; you bring down to the realm of the dead and bring up again.
But a human being kills through his own wickedness, and the departed spirit does not return, nor is the breath that has been taken captive released.
For it is impossible to escape from your hand.
The ungodly refused to acknowledge you, but they were tormented by the strength of your arm, pursued by extraordinary showers of hail and inescapable crashes, and consumed by fires.
And the new and marvelous thing was that fire worked even more powerfully in water, which extinguishes everything, for the world fights on behalf of the righteous.
At times the flame grew gentle so that it would not burn the animals sent against the ungodly, but they watched and saw that they were being thrown into confusion by God's judgment.
And at times, in the midst of water, it blazed beyond the usual strength of fire, so that it might destroy the produce of the sinful land.
In contrast, you provided your people with the food of angels and gave them ready-made bread from heaven without their having to labor, sufficient for every desire and suited to every taste.
For your sustenance showed your sweetness toward your children, serving the desire of the one receiving it and changing into whatever anyone wished.
Snow and ice withstood fire and did not melt, so that we might know that the fire destroyed the produce of the enemies, blazing amid the hail and flashing in the midst of water.
And that same fire, in turn, forgot its own strength so that the righteous might be fed.
For your creation serves you, its Creator, and grows fierce to punish the unrighteous, and is blessed to do good on behalf of those who trust in you.
Therefore, even then, changing into every form, it served your gift that nourishes all, according to the wishes of your people who were in need.
This was so that your children, whom you loved, Lord, might learn that it is not the produce of crops that nourishes a person, but your word that preserves those who believe in you.
For what was not destroyed by fire quickly melted when warmed by the faint rays of the sun.
This was to make it clear that one must rise before the sun to praise you and come before you before the light dawns.
For the hope of the ungrateful will melt like winter frost and flow away like useless water.
For your judgments are great and hard to explain; therefore, souls without instruction went astray.
The lawless thought they could oppress the holy nation, but, bound by darkness and fettered by a long night, shut up beneath their roofs, they lay fallen, fugitives from eternal providence.
For they thought they were hiding with their secret sins, but beneath the lightless veil of their folly they were scattered, utterly bewildered, terrified, and troubled.
For not even the darkness that held them kept them free from fear: noises echoing around them stunned them, and grim apparitions with unsmiling faces appeared.
No force of fire could give light, nor could blazing flames kindled by fire succeed in brightening the gloomy night.
Only a fire burning on its own appeared to them, full of terror. Frightened by that unseen vision, they thought it even worse than what they saw.
They fell into the deceptions of the magical arts, and a humiliating rebuke fell upon their arrogant schemes.
For those who promised to drive terrors and disturbances from the souls of the afflicted were themselves afflicted with a laughable fear.

For although nothing extraordinary frightened them, they panicked at the passing of crawling creatures and the hissing of reptiles and perished trembling, refusing even to look at the air, which could nowhere be escaped.
For wickedness is a cowardly thing: condemned by its own testimony and tormented by conscience, it always anticipates unbearable things.
For fear is nothing but the abandonment of the help that reason offers.
While the expectation within is slight, it considers the uncertainty greater than the causes that bring on the torments.
And they slept the same sleep through that dreadful, unbearable night, which had come upon them from the inaccessible darkness of Hades.
At times they were terrified by apparitions in their visions, and at times they fainted as their spirits failed them, for fear came upon them suddenly and unexpectedly.
Then whoever was there at the time remained there, held captive in a prison without iron bars.
Whether he was a farmer, a shepherd, or a worker laboring in the wilderness, he was seized and fell into inescapable distress.
For they were all bound with one chain of darkness. Whether a wind blew, or the sweet voices of birds sounded among thick branches, or rushing waters flowed violently,

or threatening rocks rumbled as they tumbled, or unseen animals rushed about and leaped, or wild beasts roared terribly, or echoes rebounded from caves in the mountains, these unnerved them and filled them with terror.
For the whole world shone brightly with light and stood firm, unhindered in its work.
But over them alone a heavy night was spread, an image of the darkness that was to receive them; yet they were a heavier burden to themselves than the darkness was.
But your holy ones had a great light. The others heard their voices but did not see their forms; even those who suffered such torments called them blessed.
And they were thankful that those who had previously been wronged did not harm them, and they begged them to leave.
In place of this, a pillar of flame led them along the unfamiliar road; you gave them a harmless sun for their generous hospitality.
For they deserved to be deprived of light and confined in darkness, since they kept your children imprisoned, through whom the life-giving light of the imperishable law was to be given to the world.

For they had planned to slaughter the infants of the holy ones, and when one child had been cast out and saved, you slew and destroyed the multitude of their children in retribution, and destroyed them all together in the raging waters.
That night was made known beforehand to our fathers, so that, seeing with certainty the oaths in which they had trusted, they might take courage.
Your people awaited the deliverance of the righteous and the destruction of their enemies.
For by the same means with which you punished our adversaries, you called us to yourself and glorified us.

For the children of noble men offered sacrifices in secret and unanimously pledged themselves to the law of holiness, to share alike in the blessings and sufferings of the holy ones; there, Father, they sang sweet praise.
But over there, in contrast, the discordant cry of their enemies rang out, and a pitiful sound arose from the mourning for their children.
In the same way, servants were tormented along with their masters, and the common people suffered the same things as the king.
All alike, struck by the same kind of death, had countless dead, and the living were not even sufficient to bury them, for in a single moment their noble offspring were destroyed.
For they had believed nothing because of their sorceries, but at the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged them to be your people.
While peace enveloped everything, and the swiftly passing night was halfway through its course,
your almighty word came from heaven, from the royal throne, like a fierce warrior into the midst of the doomed land.
Bearing your impartial command as a steel sword, it entered and filled everything with death. It brushed against heaven above and reached the earth below.
Then terrifying visions in dreams immediately troubled them, and unexpected terrors came upon them.
One here and another there fell half dead, making known the reason why he was dying.
For the dreams that troubled them foretold this, so that they would not perish without knowing why they were being so cruelly tormented.
At one time a trial of death also came upon the righteous, and a multitude was destroyed in the wilderness. But your anger did not last long.
For the blameless man hurried forward into the battle, bringing atonement with the weapons of his ministry—prayer and incense. He stood against the anger and put an end to the blows,

showing that he was your servant. He overcame the great multitude, not by bodily strength or by the power of weapons, but subdued the tormentor with a word, recalling the oaths and covenants made with the fathers.
Standing among the heaps of corpses that had fallen upon one another, he stopped the anger and cut a path between the living and the dead.
For the whole universe was on his ankle-length robe, and the glory of the fathers was engraved on the four rows of stones, and your majesty was a crown upon their heads.
The destroyer recoiled from these things and was terrified by them, for the trial of anger alone was enough.
But merciless wrath came upon the ungodly to the very end, for he knew even what they would do in the future:
that they would change their minds about the departure and, after sending them away in haste, would regret it and pursue them.

For while they were still occupied with their mourning and crying out at the graves of the dead, they devised yet another foolish plan. Those whom they had begged to leave and sent away, they pursued as fugitives.
For the distress they deserved was drawing them toward that end, and they forgot what had happened to them, so that they would undergo the full punishment of the sufferings still to come,
and your people would travel a wonderfully new path, while they would meet a new and strange death.
For all creation, in each of its orders, was renewed afresh to serve your commands, so that [?] children might be kept unharmed.
The cloud would cover the camp, and the dry ground beneath the water appeared. In the Red Sea there was an unobstructed path, and in place of the violent whirlpools, a flowering plain.
Through it they passed together, sheltered by your hand, seeing wondrous deeds.
For they pranced like horses and leaped like lambs, praising you, Lord, who had saved them.

For they still remembered what had happened during their stay in a foreign land: how, instead of the birth of animals, their land brought forth [?], and instead of aquatic creatures, the river brought forth a multitude of frogs.
Afterward they also saw a new brood of birds, when, driven by longing, they asked for delicacies to eat.

For quails came up from the sea to comfort them, and punishments came upon the sinners, not without signs that had appeared beforehand, with the force of raging thunderbolts. For they rightly suffered according to their own wickedness, because they had devised a cruel hatred of foreigners.
For some did not welcome the strangers who came, while the others enslaved guests who had benefited them.
And not only this, but punishment will also come upon them because they received foreigners with hatred.
But those who had welcomed them with joyful celebrations, and with whom they had long enjoyed the same rights, tortured them with unbearable suffering.
They were struck with blindness, like those at the righteous man's doors, when they were surrounded by lightless, impenetrable darkness, and each searched for the way out through his own doorway.

For on their account the elements were harmonized as on a harp: each, with its own tuned sounds, sounded its own name, always remaining in the same tone. This can truly be inferred from the sight of what happened.
For land creatures changed into water creatures, and swimming creatures became land creatures.
Fire overcame water by its own power, and water forgot its own extinguishing nature.

And the flames, as they moved about, did not scorch the flesh of animals that were easily consumed, nor did they melt the ice-like substance of the sweet food that melted easily. For in everything you exalted your people and glorified them, and you did not neglect them at any time or in any place, protecting them, Lord. The Wisdom of Solomon is completed.
